title: Buttermilk Fried Chicken
subtitle: Crispy Southern-style fried chicken
excerpt: Chicken pieces soaked overnight in spiced buttermilk, then fried in a seasoned flour coating until deeply golden and crisp. The buttermilk keeps the meat juicy all the way through.

recipe.sourceNotes: Buttermilk fried chicken is one of the defining dishes of the American South. The technique of soaking chicken in buttermilk before frying has roots in Southern cooking that predate the Civil War, and it appears in American regional cookbooks throughout the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.

recipeTools.notes: Or a large deep saucepan with a thermometer.
For checking oil and meat temperature.

content.text: Buttermilk fried chicken is chicken soaked in spiced buttermilk for at least four hours, then dredged in seasoned flour and fried until the coating is deeply golden and the meat is cooked through. The buttermilk does two things: it tenderises the meat and gives the coating something to grip. The result is crunchy on the outside and juicy all the way to the bone.

Mix the buttermilk with the hot sauce, garlic powder, smoked paprika, and 1 teaspoon of the salt. Add the chicken pieces and turn to coat. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Mix the flour with the cornstarch, the remaining salt, onion powder, cayenne, and black pepper in a wide, shallow dish.

Lift each piece of chicken from the buttermilk, letting the excess drip off. Press firmly into the flour mixture on all sides, then shake off any loose flour. Place on a wire rack and leave for 10 minutes for the coating to set.

Heat the oil in a large deep saucepan or deep fryer to 175 C. Fry the chicken in batches of three or four pieces, without crowding, for 12 to 15 minutes until the coating is deep golden and an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part reads 74 C. Larger pieces may need up to 18 minutes.
Drain on a wire rack set over a baking tray, not on kitchen paper, so the base stays crisp. Season with a little extra salt while still hot and serve.
